card.name: Yuka
card.tagline: Cuban-Congo (Bantu) secular drum-dance, ancestor of rumba.
card.profile: Yuka is a secular Afro-Cuban tradition of drumming, singing and dancing developed in western Cuba (Matanzas, Pinar del Rio) by enslaved Kongo (Bantu) people during colonial times. The Bantu word yuka means 'to beat' and also names the three drums used (caja, mula, and the smallest). The secular couple dance is a stylized courtship contest - the man pursues, the woman avoids - featuring the vacunao pelvic thrust and movements imitating roosters and hens. Yuka predates rumba and gave rise to the yambu style; it survives in Kongo communities of Pinar del Rio (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: Yuka (with Abakua) is one of the principal African roots of Cuban rumba, and its drums are considered direct ancestors of the conga/tumbadora (English Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: A Kongo rumba antecedent. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Cuba.
